summary:
The sector layers stand on firm ground for the Arab term, on softer ground for the haredi shock, and the Arab capacity ceiling is looser than the data allow.

Arab turnout. The official series (Bayan 28) runs from 75% in 1999 to the mid-50s, then 63.5 (2015), 49.2 / 59.2 / 64.8 (2019-20), 44.6 (2021) and 53.2 (2022). Peer-reviewed work (Hitman 2021; Rudnitzky 2022; Rosenthal, Zubida & Nachmias 2017) explains the swings by list unity and perceived political efficacy, and 2022 shows the unity rule is conditional. The Central Elections Committee moved to disqualify Arab lists or candidates in most elections since 2003, the Court always reversed it, and turnout moved both ways afterwards, so there is no backlash term to add. The 2025-26 KAP/Stat-Net surveys bracket the model: 53% if the parties run separately, 62-67% if all four reunite. But survey-based turnout forecasts have missed by 4-15 points in both directions (KAP 2021 +15; Statnet for Kan, Aug 2022, -14; KAP Oct 2022 -4), and stated intention runs 15-35 points above reality. That vindicates the s.20 decision not to drive the dial from surveys. The 0.58 mean sits inside the pre-registered band, but three of its four years are four-party-unity years. 2026's structure has one precedent (2021, 44.6%), and both prime-ministerial candidates exclude Arab parties, which the efficacy literature reads as a demobiliser. The stakes are small: through k = 0.247, 0.53 vs 0.58 is about 0.25 seats. The site sentence calling 2021 a 'split year' contradicts the 58% it sits inside.

How polls see the sector. The 2026 CEC filings show mostly Hebrew online panels of 500-610 with low response. Tatika's raw sample is 11% Arab, about the 2022 voter share and far below the ~16% electorate share. Channel 13 alone runs a separate StatNet phone sample of Arabs. INES had to add Arabic phone interviews because online panels yield too few Arabs. Houses embed different turnouts: Lazar about 0.5, Afkar 0.60, Channel 13 13-15 seats. The record fits the graded term: polls under-count Arab lists by 0.69 seats on average and absorbed most swings (2021's collapse was caught; the 2022 rise was missed when the consensus expected the low 40s). The under-count is Ra'am-shaped. KAP concedes its surveys miss the Negev Bedouin, and final polls under-counted Ra'am by 2.3 seats (2021) and 0.6 (2022), yet the model moves the Joint List and Ra'am together.

Haredi. The population grows 4.2% a year (IDI 2025). Turnout is flat, about 76% at regular stations and about 79% with envelopes; 2022 was a rebound, not a surge. Under-coverage is real: 69% internet use vs 94%, online response rates of 3.6-26%, and a pre-2015 audit found haredi parties under-polled. The -1.35 magnitude is fragile, though: the raw mean is -0.98, the last four cycles -0.58, and the mean without April 2019 is -0.92. April 2019 had a structural cause (Yahad's late withdrawal). About 90% of the under-poll is Shas, not UTJ. The 17 Sept High Court ban on real-time voter tracking weakens the machine that produced past beats. Realised haredi-list growth is about +1 seat per term, not +1.5-2.

Capacity. KALPI_ARAB_CAP implicitly assumes a 100% Arab-list share and 0.78 concentration. Measured values (at most 0.94, and 0.81-0.85) put the bound near 15%. The 15 Oct draws give 19 or more Arab seats in 10.7% of simulations, which would need record-breaking turnout. The haredi floor is a judgement bound that binds in under 1% of draws.

Druze turnout is falling and Druze barely appear in samples. Yisrael Beytenu's record shows no FSU poll bias. Envelopes add about 10 points to settlement turnout.

findings.claim: The official Arab-and-Druze turnout series swings far more than national turnout, and the 2022 base the model scales from is a regular-station figure. Reuses atlas D2-F02 (verified with corrections) and D2-F07.
findings.quant: Arab and Druze towns, % of eligible (regular stations, no double envelopes): 1999 75.0, 2003 62.0, 2006 56.3, 2009 53.4, 2013 56.5, 2015 63.5, Apr 2019 49.2, Sep 2019 59.2, 2020 64.8, 2021 44.6, 2022 53.2 (Bayan 28, Figure 1). 2022: 938,401 eligible, 498,894 voters; Arab lists 85.8% of these votes (423,877), Jewish parties 14.2% (70,118) (Table 2). Regions 2022: North 53.9, Triangle 52.5, Negev 51.0. Gap to national turnout 3.7-22.8 points (atlas correction). Project kalpi cluster 'arab' (839,273 eligible, 2022) measures 0.538, the model's ARAB_TURNOUT base.

The April 2019 miss had a structural cause: Yahad's late withdrawal and a record wasted vote, on top of young first-time voters. Without that cycle, or on the raw scale, or in the last four cycles, the mean is -0.6 to -1.0.

findings.claim: The election-day machine that produced past haredi over-performance is constrained in 2026. The High Court unanimously barred party polling-station agents from passing who-has-voted data to their parties. The Likud and the ultra-Orthodox parties had relied on that data heavily.
findings.quant: Ruling of 17 Sep 2026 (Justice Willner, with Stein and Kabub). It overturned the full Committee's decision allowing the practice; per other press reports, not opened, that decision had reversed chairman Sohlberg's August ban. Grounds: no legal authority, and a breach of the Protection of Privacy Law. Per the same unopened reports, the CEC will publish aggregate per-station turnout during the day. No quantitative estimate of the GOTV effect exists.

findings.claim: The Arab capacity ceiling is loose. Its formula implicitly assumes every Arab-town voter backs an Arab list and uses a 0.78 concentration. Measured values (at most 94% in-sector Arab-list share; concentration 0.81-0.85) and 2020's record, scaled to the 72% maximum turnout, put the physical bound near 14.8-15.4% of the vote, not 16.3%. Turnout must be compared on one basis: envelopes add about 3 points to Arab and 7.5-10 points to Jewish and settlement turnout (atlas D2-F04).
findings.quant: Project kalpi 'arab' cluster (CEC locality results): eligible 757,660 / 767,421 / 779,315 / 804,615 / 839,273; turnout 0.485 / 0.599 / 0.660 / 0.445 / 0.538; in-sector Arab-list share 0.790 / 0.873 / 0.942 / 0.880 / 0.931; concentration 0.852 / 0.845 / 0.829 / 0.821 / 0.813 (2019a-2022). Record: Arab lists 12.67% of all votes in 2020 at 0.660. Cap formula: 839k x 0.72 / 0.78 / 4.79M = 16.3%; with share 0.942 and concentration 0.813 on a 2026 cluster of about 940k eligible and 5.1-5.3M votes, about 14.8-15.4%. Production draws (15 Oct): P(Arab seats >= 19) 10.7%, >= 20 6.1%, 95th percentile 20; given Ra'am passes, Arab sd 3.09 seats vs a final-poll family error sd of 1.45. Envelope basis: Arab localities 53.2 -> 56.0%, Jewish/mixed 73.0% with envelopes, Judea and Samaria 75.3 -> 85.3% (atlas D2-F04). Max Arab+Druze turnout on record 75.0% (1999); central Arab localities 75.6% (2020).

challenges.title: Haredi family mean: shrink toward the raw and recent record, and allocate it to Shas
challenges.what_literature_says: Haredi under-coverage is real: low internet use, low online response, and a pre-2015 audit finding haredi parties under-estimated (SEC-F15, F18). But the magnitude is fragile. The raw mean is -0.98; the last four cycles are -0.58 raw and -0.74 e1; without Apr 2019 it is -0.92 (SEC-F20). Apr 2019 had a structural cause (Yahad's late withdrawal and a record wasted vote; Malach). About 90% of the raw under-poll is Shas (-0.88 vs UTJ -0.10), consistent with Shas's non-haredi masorti base (SEC-F19). 2022 was a turnout rebound, not a surge (SEC-F17). The 2026 GOTV-tracking ban weakens the election-day machine (SEC-F21). Pollsters now run dedicated haredi samples, and Project 61 warned that house corrections lapse when methods change.
challenges.current_model: FAMILY_SHOCK['haredi'] = (-1.352, 1.768) seats (e1 mean over 8 cycles), applied to Shas and UTJ in proportion to base share. Site: 'haredi lists underpolled by 1.35 ± 1.77 seats'. Dossier s.34 attributes the beat to '2022's haredi turnout surge'.
challenges.proposed_change: Grade three arms: (a) the e0 mean (-0.98); (b) a shrunk or recency-weighted mean (for example, 50% shrinkage toward the last-four-cycle -0.6); (c) list-weighted allocation, with each list's share of the family mean set by its own lineage record (Shas about 90%, UTJ about 10%) instead of base share. Keep the sd. Correct the s.34 sentence: the record shows a rebound to the 2019-20 turnout level.
challenges.how_to_test: Strict leave-one-cycle-out harness (validate_bayes), pooled across the 3 seeds at eve, D-7 and D-21: median and mean MAE, list-level MAE for Shas and UTJ, threshold Brier, interval score; shipping rule as in s.36. Report the 2026 effect on the NB seat mean and P(NB>=61). Evidence class: own measurement plus IDI demographic data.

challenges.title: Arab turnout mean 0.58 leans on four-party-unity years; 2026's structure points lower
challenges.what_literature_says: Unity raises turnout only conditionally (Hitman 2021; Rudnitzky 2022). 2026 is a partial reunion whose one precedent, 2021, ran at 44.6%. The KAP separate-lists scenario is 53% (Nov 2025, May 2026). Efficacy theory (Rosenthal et al. 2017) predicts abstention when both PM candidates exclude Arab parties, as in 2026. Disqualification fights show no consistent backlash upside (SEC-F05). Survey forecasts carry errors of 4-15 points and cannot settle the question (SEC-F07, F08).
challenges.current_model: ARAB_TURNOUT['mean_unified'] = 0.580 = mean of 2015, 2019s, 2020 (four-party Joint List) and 2021 (Joint List without Ra'am), regime table B. Site text calls 2021's 45% a 'split year' although it is inside the 58% mean.
challenges.proposed_change: Keep 0.58 (it is inside the s.4 pre-registered band and is only worth about 0.25 seats through k = 0.247). Publish a sensitivity with a structural table C: 2021 plus the non-unity years 2009, 2013, 2019a and 2022, mean 0.515. Rewrite the site sentence: '58% is the mean of 2015, Sept 2019 and 2020 (all four parties on one list) and 2021 (the 2026 structure: Hadash-Ta'al-Balad together, Ra'am alone)'.
challenges.how_to_test: Harness arm arab_regC (table C, LOO) against the shipped arab_regB on the pooled route. Also a production sensitivity at T_mean 0.53 / 0.58 / 0.62 reporting Arab seats, Ra'am pass and P(NB>=61). Evidence class: own measurement plus survey brackets.

challenges.title: The ratio's base should be the polls' implied turnout, not 2022's
challenges.what_literature_says: Houses differ: Lazar's numbers imply roughly 0.50-0.53, Afkar converts at 0.60, and Channel 13's sector-weighted conversion gives 13-15 Arab seats (SEC-F13). Online panels carry 11% Arab respondents, about the 2022 voter share, while Channel 13 samples Arabs separately (SEC-F11, F12).
challenges.current_model: r = 1 + k (T_mean / 0.538 - 1) + (T - T_mean) / 0.538, on the assumption that 'national panels weight the Arab sector to the last election's turnout'.
challenges.proposed_change: Estimate the poll average's implied Arab turnout, either from filings with sector columns (Ch13 raw Arab column x population weight vs seats) or from each house's Arab total relative to its Jewish turnout. Use that as the base, or let base vary by house through the house-effect layer. Expected 2026 effect at most 0.3 seats.
challenges.how_to_test: Reconstruct implied turnout per house for 2019-2022 from archived seat tables and CEC 2022 filings; regress each house's Arab-family error on (realised / implied) turnout. If the slope beats the common-base k on LOO, adopt it. Evidence class: CEC filings plus own measurement.

challenges.title: Within the Arab family, the under-count belongs to Ra'am
challenges.what_literature_says: Sector surveys miss Ra'am's Negev Bedouin base (KAP's own caveat). Sector pollsters' Ra'am scenarios failed in 2021, and KAP under-forecast Ra'am in 2022. Final polls under-counted Ra'am by 2.29 seats (2021) and 0.57 (2022) while over-counting the Joint List in 2021 (SEC-F10).
challenges.current_model: The turnout term and the -0.634 intercept move the Joint List and Ra'am together by base share. Ra'am pass 0.752; Ra'am LOYAL_SD 1.8. The harness merges 2021 JL+Ra'am (s.43 disclosure i).
challenges.proposed_change: After the harness splits the 2021 block, grade an allocation that places the intercept on Ra'am in proportion to its Negev/under-covered share (for example, two-thirds Ra'am). Alternatively, give Ra'am a small positive own mean, and leave the turnout scaling proportional.
challenges.how_to_test: Harness (ballot-fidelity) arm on 2021 and 2022, plus the threshold Brier for Ra'am. n=2, so require no loss on pooled metrics and report as disclosed judgement if it ships. Evidence class: own measurement plus sector-survey caveats.

challenges.title: Kalpi capacity bounds: tighten the Arab ceiling; relabel the haredi floor
challenges.what_literature_says: On the project's own CEC locality data, Arab lists never took more than 94% of the Arab cluster's vote. Their concentration is 0.81-0.85, not 0.78. The 2020 record (12.67% of the vote at 66% cluster turnout), scaled to a 72% turnout ceiling and 2026 electorate growth, gives about 14.8-15.4% (SEC-F25). Shas and UTJ draw only 28% of their vote from the haredi cluster, so the 6.6% floor is a judgement bound; it binds in under 1% of draws.
challenges.current_model: KALPI_ARAB_CAP = 0.163 (839k x 0.72 / 0.78, implicitly a 100% Arab-list share). KALPI_HAREDI_FLOOR = 0.066. Site: 'each condition prunes ~1.5% of draws' (1 Sept audit). 15 Oct draws: Arab >= 19 seats in 10.7%, >= 20 in 6.1%.
challenges.proposed_change: Re-derive the cap as eligible_2026 x 0.72 x 0.94 / 0.813 / projected total votes, about 0.150 (range 0.148-0.154). Re-measure and restate the prune rates. Describe the haredi floor as a judgement floor, or retire it, since LOYAL_SD already bounds the haredi lists.
challenges.how_to_test: Backtest the cap formula, computed from the previous cycle's data only, on 2019s-2022 (no realised Arab total may exceed it). Count clipped draws in production. Report the Arab 95th percentile and the P(NB>=61) change. The capacity layer is outside the harness by construction (site annex). Evidence class: official CEC data.

challenges.title: Demographic drift claim in s.4 overstates the haredi per-cycle gain
challenges.what_literature_says: Population growth is 4.2% a year, but realised Shas+UTJ share rose about 0.2 points a year from 1992 to 2022 (about +1 seat per four-year term), and UTJ realises about 95% of its demographic growth (SEC-F16). Polls weighted to current population carry the growth already; only past-vote weighting would lag it.
challenges.current_model: Dossier s.4: 'haredi pool +1.5-2 seats (mechanical)'. It is not a parameter, but it is cited as a reason for the haredi shock's sign.
challenges.proposed_change: Restate as 'about +1 seat per four-year term; 2022->2026 about +1 (partly offset by leakage visible in the 2026 haredi samples)'. Do not use it to justify the family mean.
challenges.how_to_test: Documentation change. Optionally, regress final-poll haredi error on years since the previous election to test whether polls lag demography. Evidence class: IDI/CBS data plus own measurement.

open_questions: What Arab (and haredi) turnout does Channel 13's 'sector weights in the population' conversion (Prof. David Steinberg) assume? The same question applies to Kantar's and Lazar's online-panel weighting. Ask for the methodology notes; they set the base the turnout ratio should use.

Afkar has no public turnout or seat track record that this desk could locate. IDI has used Afkar for fieldwork (Sept 2022 special survey; 2026 first-time voters, Arab n=154). Can the firm's 2021/2022 pre-election seat estimates be obtained?

As of 15 Oct no KAP, IDI or Stat-Net turnout survey was found from after the Joint List re-formed (24 Aug) or the Supreme Court ruling (2 Oct). KAP published final pre-election surveys about a week out in 2021 and 2022 (14 Mar 2021; 25 Oct 2022). Watch for one around 20 Oct, and remember its error record (SEC-F07).
Will The Haredi Public (7.2-7.8% of Ch13's haredi samples; 0.06 expected seats in the model) withdraw or collapse into UTJ and Shas, as Yahad did in April 2019?
Size of the GOTV-tracking ban effect: no quantitative evidence exists. The CEC's aggregate per-station turnout releases may partly substitute for it.
Jewish votes for Ra'am via Segalovitz bypass the Arab-sector arithmetic behind KALPI_ARAB_CAP; there is no measurement of their size.

In the 15 Oct production draws Shas is at zero seats in 0.35% of draws and UTJ in 0.18%, even though the floor holds (the floor bounds the sum, not each list). Is that intended, given each list's LOYAL_SD and record?
The site's claim that each capacity condition 'prunes ~1.5% of draws' dates from the 1 Sept audit and should be re-measured. The haredi floor now appears to bind in well under 1%.

Direct measures of 2022 Druze and FSU turnout were not found. Nir Atmor's 2026 Springer chapter 'Divided We Stand: The Electoral System and Voter Turnout in Israel, 2019-2022' (doi 10.1007/978-981-95-3704-4_16) may contain them; it was not opened and is unverified.

Expert expectations reported in the press for 2026 range from roughly 40-60% (Rudnitzky, quoted by the Jewish Chronicle, 14 Oct 2026) to about 65% (Jonathan Mendel, same article). These are news-reported judgements, not data, so they were not used as findings.
